title_short: Angela Harrell · AYH · Kindness and Care Really Matter
headline: A Soles4Souls board member says shoes break the cycle of poverty, and that her happiness comes from giving back.
story: Angela has served on the Soles4Souls board for six years. She says they break the cycle of poverty through things some of us take for granted: shoes and clothing.
Asked if she is happy, she says yes. The source is the ability to give back and serve others.
In the United States, 1.5 million kids face homelessness. New shoes let them hold their head up a little higher and blend in. Her message: kindness and care really matter.

--- NNM_3559.MXF ---
[00:02.6] So, can you tell me your name and what you at Voya?
[00:08.6] My name is Angela Harrell and I am the Senior Vice President, Chief Purpose Talent and Inclusion Officer as well as the President of Voya Foundation.
[00:25.8] So I chose to spend the morning volunteering here today with my colleagues from Voya Financial as a component of our employee volunteer sabbatical with Soles4Souls that we have every single year.
[00:40.3] I also happen to be on the board of Soles4Souls.
[00:44.0] I've served on the board for six years and so this non-profit is near and dear to my heart.
[00:50.3] Why is it near and dear to your heart?
[00:53.0] So Soles4Souls is near and dear to my heart because they are impacting people's lives in a really significant and simple way.
[01:01.8] They're breaking the cycle of poverty through the things that some of us take for granted, shoes and clothing.
[01:09.4] And so one of the things that we are able to do is enable economic empowerment through the collection of used or new shoes and clothing.
[01:21.7] The thing go to entrepreneurs in other countries where they're able to resell and take care of their family, their needs.
[01:29.7] And so it's a small thing.
[01:31.3] We're here today sorting donated shoes that have been gently used, making sure that we've got pairs, that we're binding them together and we're packing them up for the next part of their journey.
[01:45.8] And why do you think this work is so important?
[01:52.4] I think this work is so important because it's providing people with an opportunity.
[01:57.5] In fact, the program name is 4Opportunity.
[02:01.9] We're providing people with the means to take care of themselves, to empower their families economically through our collection of used shoes and clothing, individuals are able to resell these in low income nations and take care of their family's most pressing needs.
[02:21.5] Okay.
[02:22.5] Can you talk a little bit more about the 4EveryKid since you guys are doing that tomorrow?
[02:26.9] Yes.
[02:29.0] 4EveryKid is an amazing program where we work with schools and nonprofits across the country to put a new pair of branded athletic shoes on the feet of children who are experiencing homelessness. [also in the “Where Are My Jordans?” cut]
[02:45.9] And believe it or not, in the United States, that's 1.5 million kids. [also in the “Where Are My Jordans?” cut]
[02:52.2] And in doing this, it provides them with a level playing field. [also in the “Where Are My Jordans?” cut]
[02:56.9] All kids just want to be like everyone else. [also in the “Where Are My Jordans?” cut]
[02:59.4] And so a branded pair of sneakers perhaps allows them to try out for the basketball team or run track or really just get to school comfortably and safely. [also in the “Where Are My Jordans?” cut]
[03:10.8] And more than anything else, it allows them to hold their head up a little bit higher and blend in because that's all you really want to do as a kid anyway. [also in the “Where Are My Jordans?” cut]
[03:19.3] Awesome.
[03:23.7] And then how does doing this work make you feel and how do you feel after today?
[03:29.9] Yeah.
[03:31.6] So doing this work makes me feel such a sense of gratitude.
[03:36.5] One, to be able to, through my company, volunteer.
[03:49.5] Community is really important.
[03:51.6] Going back for me is so central to who I am as an individual.
[03:57.6] Why I really love this work is because I've had the ability to see everything along the chain from the collection of shoes, which I do myself, throughout the year, to seeing those shoes in a warehouse being sorted.
[04:13.6] And then getting to our nonprofit partners outside of the United States, which I've been able to do in Guatemala and Honduras and in the Dominican Republic.
[04:23.2] And then seeing the individuals who actually get those shoes, being able to meet with those people and understand how this is actually changing their lives and the lives of their families.
[04:35.5] What's gorgeous is other employees of Voya being able to experience parts of this story as well.
[04:43.9] And so that's what really just fills my heart and gives me such gratitude that we have this chance to serve.
[04:51.1] And this service has such a significant impact.
[05:03.7] I am so excited for tomorrow.
[05:05.7] My favorite thing about Soles4Souls is distribution.
[05:09.8] I love when we have kids excited about their new pair of branded shoes.
[05:19.2] Sometimes we get some really tough customers who are very specific. [do not use: do not use: the “Where Are My Jordans?” cut uses this]
[05:22.3] They're like, where are my Jordans? [do not use: do not use: the “Where Are My Jordans?” cut uses this]
[05:24.1] Do you have any Nikes? [do not use: do not use: the “Where Are My Jordans?” cut uses this]
[05:26.5] But in the end, everyone leaves happy. [do not use: do not use: the “Where Are My Jordans?” cut uses this]
[05:29.3] Some kids want to wear their shoes right out. [do not use: do not use: the “Where Are My Jordans?” cut uses this]
[05:31.8] Some kids want to put them in a box, keep them brand new and take them home to share with their families just the thrill of these new pair of shoes. [do not use: do not use: the “Where Are My Jordans?” cut uses this]
[05:42.4] And so that is what is so exciting, that we get that opportunity to put some smiles and some pep and steps for kids at school.
[05:54.0] And we really will have a chance also as employees of Voya to experience something together that I think is really special and impactful.
--- NNM_3560.MXF ---
[00:03.9] This is the Are You Happy block.
[00:06.4] And so, super simple question, are you happy?
[00:09.7] Yes. [do not use: she checks what to say]
[00:11.5] Am I supposed to say yes, I'm happy? [do not use: she checks what to say]
[00:14.0] Yes. [do not use: she checks what to say]
[00:14.0] Okay. [do not use: she checks what to say]
[00:14.7] Yes, I'm happy.
[00:16.5] Okay, and then what is the source of your happiness?
[00:19.9] The source of my happiness is the ability to give back and to serve others.
[00:26.9] And tell me a little bit more about that.
[00:32.7] How giving back makes me happy is, oh.
[00:37.0] Giving back makes me happy.
[00:38.2] Oh, giving back?
[00:39.4] Okay.
[00:40.9] Giving back makes me happy because it really provides me with a chance to kinda show love and care for people.
[00:49.5] Sometimes people I know, sometimes people I don't.
[00:52.8] But I feel like I have been so fortunate in my life and it gives me the ability to pull others kind of who are in need up a step as well.
[01:03.5] And so, I love the ability to give back.
[01:07.7] And then if you could send one message to the entire world, what would that message be?
[01:13.7] If I could send one message to the entire world, it would be that kindness and care really matter.
[01:22.6] Really matters.
[01:23.9] And so, it's something that each one of us absolutely have the ability to give.
[01:29.7] It's not about economics, it's not about politics, it's not about anything except for kindness.
[01:36.4] Work of this nature allows you to put that to the test.
[01:41.1] Volunteerism and service allows you to put kindness and care into something significant, but it can also be something small and simple, like a smile, like a thank you, like sharing gratitude to someone, like opening the door.
[01:60.0] Kindness and care is something throughout the course of your day, practice it.
[02:04.9] It'll make you feel incredible and it'll make the people around you feel incredible too.
